ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Posterior shoulder dislocation: 5

A posterior shoulder dislocation remained unrecognized for weeks and produced substantial articular injury. Years later, the patient has pain, stiffness and joint-space narrowing. Which delayed complication best links the old injury to the current degeneration?

  1. Acute compartment syndrome
  2. Post-traumatic osteoarthritis
  3. Joint stiffness
  4. Osteonecrosis
  5. Nonunion
Answer and explanation

Post-traumatic osteoarthritis

Articular incongruity or cartilage damage can cause later degenerative joint changes.

Option explanations

Post-traumatic osteoarthritis: Articular incongruity or cartilage damage can cause later degenerative joint changes.

Joint stiffness: Capsular contracture, adhesions and prolonged immobilization can restrict motion after injury. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Osteonecrosis: Disruption of blood supply can lead to death and collapse of an injured bony segment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Nonunion: Persistent failure of fracture healing requires assessment of stability, biology, infection and patient factors. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Acute compartment syndrome: Rising compartment pressure impairs perfusion; escalating pain and pain on passive stretch require urgent assessment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
